comparison: Both address the mechanistic model (C120-C122) for Cgr1-Cgr2 complex formation and electron transfer. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting the model lacks direct experimental validation but is appropriately presented as speculative. Peer reviewers also express UNCERTAINTY, questioning Cgr1's role and noting lack of in vivo validation, particularly that Rhodococcus expression without Cgr1 still permitted digoxin reduction.

Both address sequence comparison analysis showing Cgr2 represents a novel enzyme family (C101-C106). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the SSN analysis, sequence alignments, and mutagenesis validation compelling. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, explicitly stating the authors demonstrate Cgr2 is a novel family without raising concerns.

Both address heterologous expression experiments (C49-C51) showing Cgr2 sufficiency. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning Cgr1's importance and requesting discussion of other genes in the conserved cluster, noting the lack of Cgr1 expression in Rhodococcus still permitted activity.

Both address cgr gene cluster identification and conservation (C4, C30-C31, C34). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding converging evidence from strain screening, phylogenetics, and machine learning appropriate. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, finding the extreme conservation (99.95±0.05% nucleotide identity) 'puzzling' and 'highly unlikely,' requesting careful rechecking and additional controls.

Both address metagenomic prevalence analysis (C107-C112, C128-C129). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the statistical analysis and correlation with E. lenta marker appropriate. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether enzyme presence implies function, asking how to discount other enzymes metabolizing digoxin, and noting tension between widespread presence and low abundance of E. lenta.

Both address evolutionary hypotheses about host protection (C135-C136). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the hypothesis is reasonable but speculative without direct experimental support. Peer reviewers also rate as UNCERTAIN, explicitly questioning whether the enzyme carries out plant toxin detoxification in vivo and noting this fascinating possibility is not directly tested.

Both address substrate specificity findings (C90-C94). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the systematic assays with 28 compounds and statistical analysis (p<0.01) compelling. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, explicitly stating the authors demonstrate specific conversion of digoxin and closely related compounds without raising concerns.

Both address RNA-seq data on gene expression (C35-C37) and cac gene function (C125-C127). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for the differential expression data. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning the role of the cac locus that co-occurs with Cgr but doesn't turn on with digoxin, requesting discussion of other genes in the conserved cluster.

Both address cysteine mutagenesis findings (C72-C73, C74-C75). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN for C72-C73 due to contradictory findings about cysteines being important for activity but not [Fe-S] incorporation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, noting the authors narrow down which cysteines are likely involved in cluster formation without raising concerns.

Both address sequence conservation analysis (C77-C82) and Y333N variant characterization (C83-C87, C130, C139). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for both sets of claims, finding the validation by Sanger sequencing and kinetic data compelling. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, acknowledging the comparison of N333 and Y333 variants and their significance for digoxin metabolism.

Both address EPR spectroscopy and [4Fe-4S] cluster characterization (C64-C71) as part of broader biochemical characterization. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding g-values, temperature dependence, and spin quantitation consistent with [4Fe-4S]1+ centers. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, explicitly stating the authors demonstrate Cgr2 requires [4Fe-4S] clusters and FAD+ without raising concerns.

Both address protein purification and cofactor requirements (C53-C58). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the systematic troubleshooting and observations about [Fe-S] cluster reconstitution and FAD requirements clear. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED as part of the broader biochemical characterization demonstrating Cgr2 is a novel reductase.

Both address UV-vis spectroscopy data (C59-C63) showing [Fe-S] cluster characteristics. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the characteristic absorption features and oxygen sensitivity experiments appropriate. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED as part of the comprehensive biochemical characterization without raising specific concerns.

Both address growth experiments and substrate specificity (C95-C97). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the demonstration that cardenolides are not respiratory substrates clear. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, acknowledging the specific conversion of digoxin and closely related compounds without concerns about these negative results.

Both address SSN analysis showing Cgr2 uniqueness (C98-C100). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the singleton status at high stringency thresholds demonstrates uniqueness. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, stating the authors show via sequence comparisons that Cgr2 represents a novel family.

Both address metal activation assays (C74-C75). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the differential effects on cysteine mutants suggest metal coordination. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, noting the mutagenesis work narrows down cysteine involvement without raising concerns.

Both address kinetic characterization of Y333N variant (C83-C87). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED despite p=0.052 being marginally non-significant, noting clear trends and time course data. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, acknowledging the comparison of variants and their significance for metabolism.

Both address qPCR validation of prevalence (C113-C115). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the independent cohort validation strengthens conclusions. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, not specifically questioning the qPCR data but questioning the functional interpretation of presence data.

Both address the conclusion that Cgr2 is a novel enzyme (C117-C118). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on comprehensive biochemical and sequence analysis. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, explicitly stating the authors demonstrate Cgr2 is a novel reductase.

Both address prevalence data and clinical implications (C128-C129). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the inference connecting prevalence to clinical observations reasonable. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether presence implies function and noting the tension with E. lenta's low abundance.

Both address limitations regarding cac gene function (C125-C127). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the acknowledgment of uncertainties appropriate. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, explicitly questioning the role of the cac locus and requesting discussion of other genes in the conserved cluster.

Both address the importance of nucleotide-level resolution for predicting drug metabolism (C138-C139). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on Y333N variant data. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, acknowledging the significance of the two variants for digoxin metabolism.

OpenEval addresses speculation about digoxin not being the endogenous substrate (C88-C89), rating as SUPPORTED as appropriately presented speculation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific point.

OpenEval addresses established background knowledge from literature (C1-C2, C9-C17, C142-C143, C145), rating as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing background claims.

OpenEval addresses prior work by the authors (C3, C18-C24), rating as SUPPORTED as accurately summarizing foundation for current study. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these historical claims.

OpenEval addresses bioinformatic predictions about Cgr1 (C38-C48), rating as SUPPORTED with appropriate speculation about complex formation. Peer reviewers question Cgr1's role in R2 but don't specifically evaluate these bioinformatic predictions.

OpenEval addresses broader implications and future directions (C137, C140-C141, C144), rating as SUPPORTED as reasonable recommendations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these forward-looking claims.

Peer reviewers note the phylogenetic observation about cgr cassette gain and loss (C28-C29) as SUPPORTED without concerns. OpenEval addresses these claims in R1 as part of broader gene cluster identification but doesn't separately evaluate the gain/loss observation.
